title: Remove Adjacent Almost-Equal Characters
summary: Given a string, determine the least number of operations required to eliminate all adjacent characters that are almost equal.
statement: Given a string, determine the least number of operations required to eliminate all adjacent characters that are almost equal. An operation consists of changing any character to any lowercase letter. Two characters are almost equal if they are the same or adjacent in the alphabet.
constraints: word is a nonempty lowercase string.
Adjacent letters are almost equal when their alphabet positions differ by at most one.
One operation changes any character; return the minimum operations eliminating every almost-equal adjacent pair.
hints: Changing one endpoint of a conflicting adjacent pair can also neutralize the next pair.
Scan left to right; upon a conflict, change the right endpoint conceptually and skip the following comparison.
If abs(word[i]-word[i-1])<=1, add one and advance by two; otherwise advance by one.
The leftmost remaining conflict requires an edit at one endpoint, and choosing its right endpoint never harms the already-clean prefix while covering the maximum future edge.
editorial: The leftmost remaining conflict requires an edit at one endpoint, and choosing its right endpoint never harms the already-clean prefix while covering the maximum future edge.

tests.explanation: Changing the second and fourth letters to c removes all conflicts in two operations.
The pairs ab and dd can be broken with two changes; no one change touches both separated conflicts.
